synthesis: DEV-2465 replaces the zero-query stub body of the 'Unique Scans to Case Claims' Company Metrics card (already registered at cards()['unique-scans-to-case-claims'] = UniqueScansToCaseClaims::class, row 2 col 3, by DEV-2409/#394) with a real metric: the share of case-claimed vehicles our cameras had already seen before the claim, i.e. (claimed orders with >=1 pre-claim hits_cold hit) / (DEV-2463's UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery 'deduped' claim count), expressed as a percentage. Both sides of the ratio live on ClickHouse (zod.public_billing_events joined by hotlist_id into clarity.hits_cold), one connection, no PostgreSQL fallback. The card must become the first cards()-grid card to render a non-integer, must reuse (not re-port) DEV-2463's shipped denominator query, must guard the ~83%-of-orgs zero-denominator case, and must add the Pro-gate (canViewCardData) the current stub is missing. Two of the ticket's three declared 'Still open' questions (which rate; the lookback bound) are genuinely unresolved and need Oscar; the zero-state display question is answerable from an existing in-repo precedent.

scope.summary: Add a bespoke ClickHouse query class for the numerator (pre-claim hit existence per claimed order) that composes with DEV-2463's UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery for the denominator, then replace UniqueScansToCaseClaims's stub methods (getCardRate/getModelQueryForDates/getMonthlyData/currentPeriodTotal) with real implementations, adding the missing Pro-gate. No changes needed to CompanyMetricsOverview::cards() (already registered), DashboardWidget::getStatColor() (arm already present), or the two registry tests (count already 16, already lists this class) -- these are confirmed already-done, not gaps.

proposed_changes.change: NEW bespoke query class (mirrors UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery's shape: NOT a ClickhouseQuery subclass, no Throwable swallow -- a genuine zero is a normal reading for ~83% of orgs). Provide window(?orgId, start, end): array{numerator:int, denominator:int, rate:float} and monthlySeries(?orgId, through): array<'Y-m-01', array{numerator,denominator,rate}>. Denominator = UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery's 'deduped' stage (call its window()/monthlySeries(), do not re-port the claims CTE). Numerator = uniqExactIf(hotlist_id) of successful, non-insightlpr case-claim orders that have >=1 clarity.hits_cold row with scanned_at < the claim's own ts, using the same UTC-month/epoch-ts boundaries and the same insightlpr exclusion as UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery. rate = denominator > 0 ? numerator/denominator*100 : 0.0.

questions.q: Q1: which rate -- 96.6% (orders-with-pre-claim-hit / claimed orders) or 94.4% (distinct plates / dedup triples)?
questions.note: The ticket's 'Still open' section lists this as unresolved and repeats 'awaiting Oscar's confirmation' twice. Oscar's comments (39274 'option 1 is fine', 39276 the formula) confirm the CONCEPT (a rate, not a raw scan count) and PREDATE the 94.4% alternative, which came from Dalton's own 2026-09-04 measurement (39127). So Oscar has not been asked to choose between the two numeric formulas; the recommendation to build 96.6% is the author's engineering judgment (grain-consistency: orders over orders), not a ruling.

questions.q: Q2: should 'before the claim' be bounded by hotlist.lookback_days rather than admitting any prior scan?
questions.note: hotlist.lookback_days (int, default 270, PG migration 2025_06_16_141529 + zod.public_hotlist/clarity.hotlist mirrors) is real, but grep of app/Clickhouse, app/Services, app/Jobs shows ZERO existing usage as a query-time bound -- it is read only as a plain model property. Per okf/concepts/lpr-assist.md:77 it governs ONLY the Postgres find_historicals() trigger's H/Z historical-hit insertion at hotlist-create/update time and is explicitly 'not the assist attribution window'. Using it as an ad hoc CH query-time cutoff would be a NEW use, and it only ever applied to H/Z hits, not L/S live hits. No code precedent settles this.

questions.answer: Render 0.0%, never N/A and never hide. There is no cross-card seam or shared trait for this in DashboardWidget/RendersDashboardStat (grepped -- no N/A or division-guard helper exists). The one existing same-page precedent for a percentage stat with a zero-denominator guard is HotlistCount::getStats() (app/Filament/Widgets/Dashboard/HotlistCount.php:209-211): $missingPlatePercentage = 0; if ($this->totalDirect() > 0) { $missingPlatePercentage = round($this->missingPlates() / $this->totalDirect() * 100); } -- a plain PHP guard defaulting to 0, not a UI N/A state and not hiding the stat. Note this precedent lives OUTSIDE the cards() grid (HotlistCount is a separate Dashboard widget), so the ticket's claim that no cards()-grid card renders a non-integer today remains accurate.

questions.q: Q4 (undeclared, found in grounding): does 'exactly one query per resolved window' mean one ClickHouse round trip TOTAL (numerator+denominator in one statement), or is calling UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery::window() plus a separate numerator round trip acceptable?
questions.note: okf/concepts/billing-events.md measured that EACH additional CTE reference over public_billing_events is another full ~1.83GB/40M-row scan (3 refs = 5.5GB). Reusing UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery::window() as a black box means the numerator query independently re-scans public_billing_events to resolve hotlist_id per claim -- the same 2x-scan cost the KB warns about, even though it is 'reuse' at the PHP level. Combining both stages into one SQL statement would satisfy both 'one query' and 'no duplicate scan', but doing so without re-porting the claims CTE would require refactoring UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery's private static sql()/claims-CTE builder into something both classes share -- touching a QA-Complete shipped class (DEV-2463) that the inherited-decisions block does not authorize touching.

clarity.hits_cold's ClickHouse sort key is (hotlist_org_id, toYYYYMM(hit_created_at), hit_created_at, id) -- verified from database/schema/clickhouse-schema.sql -- NOT hotlist_id. A join filtered only on hotlist_id does not prune; the numerator query must ALSO filter hits_cold on hotlist_org_id (the leading sort-key column, and needed for tenant correctness anyway) to get skip-index benefit. Relying on idx_hotlist_id minmax alone is weak since hotlist_id is not physically sorted.

zod.public_billing_events is declared ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version) -- a ONE-argument engine, unlike 24 of the other 25 zod.public_* mirrors. FINAL deduplicates but does NOT drop _peerdb_is_deleted=1 tombstones on this table (PG-028); an explicit WHERE _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 is mandatory and not interchangeable with FINAL. UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery already gets this right; the new query must too.

resource_envelope.growth: public_billing_events grew from ~36.6M (ticket, measured 2026-09-04) to 38,485,175 (measured 2026-09-09) -- roughly +380k rows/day.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Not a scheduled command or PHP-side per-org loop -- a per-Filament-render, per-org-filtered aggregate query cached via Cache::flexible. Per cache-miss render: the denominator scan (via UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery) is a full ~1.83GB/40M-row scan of public_billing_events regardless of the org/date predicate (measured, unprunable -- ORDER BY id). If the numerator issues a SEPARATE round trip (Q4), that is a SECOND full scan of the same table, doubling per-render CH read cost. The hits_cold side is bounded ONLY if the query explicitly filters hotlist_org_id; the hotlist_id JOIN predicate alone does not prune. No PHP-side accumulator over production-sized data -- ClickHouse aggregates server-side, so this is NOT the DEV-2342 memory-residency class; residual risk is CH scan cost/duration (the sibling denominator query's measured contended p99 is already 9.3s).
unresolved: Whether the numerator query filters clarity.hits_cold on hotlist_org_id (the leading sort-key column) or relies solely on the hotlist_id join -- determines whether it prunes to one org's partitions or scans much more widely; verify via EXPLAIN / X-ClickHouse-Summary at build time.

Whether 'exactly one query per resolved window' requires combining numerator+denominator into a single ClickHouse statement (avoiding a second full public_billing_events scan) or whether two round trips are acceptable -- see Q4.
